correctness.rationale: For X^2=0 with rank X=2 and n>=4, a basis gives X with a single 2x2 identity superblock. Solving XY+YX=0 gives Y blocks P,Q,R,W,Z with P^2=Z^2=0 and PR+RZ=0, ZW-WP=0, PQ-QP+RW=0. Nonzero XY implies P is a nonzero square-zero 2x2 (q^2-1 choices and rank1). For any square-zero s=n-4 block Z, each R and W intertwiner space has dimension s, and the commutator map Q->PQ-QP has image the P-anticommutant, so q^2 solutions. Thus |F_X|=(q^2-1)q^(2n-6)S_{n-4}(q), with S_s the exact Gaussian image/kernel/isomorphism sum. Rank X=1 forces P=0. Independent direct finite-field block enumeration gave 12 for (q,n)=(2,4), 72 for (3,4), 48 for (2,5), without using the formula to accept Y. Characteristic two sign conventions were included.

originality.rationale: Schröer and Huang constrain XY=YX=0 and so exclude the claimed XY!=0 locus. Chen–Wang supply linear anticommuting normal forms and complex geometric varieties but do not count simultaneous square-zero nonannihilating fixed-X fibres over every finite field with first-rank criterion. The exterior algebra A=k<x,y>/(x²,y²,xy+yx) gives a plausible equivalent module-theoretic index not exhaustively ruled out.

value.rationale: Rank two is precisely the first possible nonzero product with two square-zero anticommuting generators; the exact uniform finite-field fibre factorization for all n and q isolates the first genuinely nonannihilating representation stratum, with nonobvious Jordan-type independence. This is a natural exact invariant with meaningful structural interpretation, not a tiny arbitrary matrix case.
